 Wisconsin Bald Eagle, Valkyrie, Joins Milwaukee Brewers’ World Series Crew
 Via Schlitz Audubon Nature Center 
 By 
 Emily Hannemann 
 Birds & Blooms Editorial Policies 
 Published on Oct. 22, 2026
 Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... 
 This eagle is a Milwaukee Brewers fan! Meet Valkyrie, a raptor ambassador at a Wisconsin nature center, who loves America's national pastime.
 As the city of Milwaukee, Wisconsin, readies itself to kick off the biggest event in baseball, the Milwaukee Brewers are receiving encouragement from a patriotic, feathered friend: Schlitz Audubon Nature Center’s ambassador bald eagle, Valkyrie . Here’s what to know about “Val,” including when she’ll be on the field, how she hit the home-run gig of helping the Brew Crew, and what she has to “say” to her home team as they embark on their first World Series in 44 years.
 Why Is Valkyrie Going to the World Series?
 Via Schlitz Audubon Nature Center
Valkyrie is an educational ambassador for Schlitz Audubon Nature Center — and a Milwaukee Brewers fan. 
 Those from outside Milwaukee might not know it, but Valkyrie has a history with the Brewers organization. Her handler, Schlitz Audubon Raptor Center’s Program Director Lindsay Focht , explains that they’ve been in partnership with the Milwaukee Brewers for the past two seasons. The Brewers had reached out to Schlitz Audubon in search of a bald eagle to be present during the national anthem at games, and they found their star in Valkyrie.
 This year, she’s been shining especially brightly during the postseason. “She attended the NLDS Game 1, then the NLCS Game 1, and when they won that, all of us were kind of holding our breath,” Lindsay says.
 While the Schlitz Audubon team wasn’t making any assumptions that they’d be invited for the World Series, the Brewers wanted Valkyrie along for the ride. “Fairly quickly after it was a reality that the Brewers were going to the World Series, the Brewers reached out and said, ‘Hey, what’s Valkyrie doing next Friday?’” Lindsay recalls with a laugh. “It’s been an amazing collaboration with them, and they’ve been wonderful hosts in showcasing Valkyrie.”
 Lindsay also mentions that it’s an incredible opportunity to raise awareness about Schlitz Audubon Nature Center and its raptors, and she’s grateful for that, as well.
 What Is Valkyrie’s Role at Milwaukee Brewers Games?
 Via Schlitz Audubon Nature Center
Valkyrie appears on the jumbotron during the national anthem at Brewers games. 
 As for Valkyrie’s job — which she takes very seriously — she arrives on the field with her handler at the same time as the color guard. She and Lindsay stand proud during the singing of the national anthem, during which Val’s regal likeness is projected for all to see on the jumbotron. After that, Val and Lindsay leave the area. (While Valkyrie might wish she could, it would be against MLB rules for her to help the Brewers players on the field.)
 Through the collaboration, Val has met former Brewers players, current players’ family members, fans, and members of the color guard. For Lindsay, it’s always a moving experience. “It’s patriotic with the singing of the anthem, the flag, and the bald eagle displayed above it,” she says. “It’s very touching. I think Valkyrie appreciates it, too.”
 About the Bald Eagle: Who Is Valkyrie?
 The Brewers’ beloved bald eagle is one of 16 non-releasable birds that live at Schlitz Audubon as ambassadors in the raptor program . She arrived at the nature center when she was only about five or six months old.
 Lindsay explains that while Val hatched in the wild , because she was fed by fishermen and picknickers in her habitat, she didn’t learn the crucial hunting skills necessary for eagles to survive. “She quickly made that connection of ‘people are good, and I want to be around them, and they give me all this food,’” Lindsay says. As a result, Valkyrie moved in to live at Schlitz Audubon, where she’s remained for 15 years.
 Her comfort around people, Lindsay highlights, makes her an amazing educational ambassador. “She has an extremely valuable and fulfilling lifestyle, doing this,” she says. “And rightfully so —she’s spoiled beyond belief! As she deserves, and all our birds deserve.”
 As for the Brewers? Valkyrie is, of course, a proud fan of the baseball team. While Val only speaks eagle, Lindsay knows what she would want to tell her favorite team: “Soar high and reach for the sky!”
 Next, marvel at more incredible, inspiring pictures of bald eagles .
 Author 
 Emily Hannemann 
 Emily Hannemann is a digital editor for Birds & Blooms. She holds a master's degree in magazine journalism from the University of Missouri - Columbia, as well as undergraduate degrees in journalism and English. In her spare time, she enjoys researching fun facts about corvids.
